questions.q: Which gas is primarily responsible for global warming?
questions.exp: Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) is the primary greenhouse gas responsible for global warming. It is released through burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes.

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol is related to?
questions.exp: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) is an international treaty that commits its parties to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It was the first agreement requiring industrialized nations to cut their CO₂ emissions.

questions.q: World Environment Day is celebrated on?
questions.exp: World Environment Day is celebrated on 5 June every year. It was established by the United Nations in 1972 and is the principal vehicle for encouraging awareness about environmental protection.

questions.q: The national animal of India is?
questions.exp: The Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) is the national animal of India. It was declared so in 1973. Project Tiger was launched to protect this endangered species.

The Chipko Movement (1973) was a forest conservation movement in Uttarakhand where villagers hugged trees to prevent them from being cut down. It was started by Sundarlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt.

questions.q: The full form of CITES is?
opts: Convention on Illegal Trade in Endangered Species
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
Committee on International Trade in Endangered Species
Convention on Illegal Tourism and Endangered Species
questions.exp: CITES stands for Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora. It is an international agreement between governments to regulate trade in wildlife species.

questions.q: Ozone layer is found in which layer of atmosphere?
questions.exp: The ozone layer is found in the stratosphere, approximately 15–35 km above Earth's surface. It absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation, protecting life on Earth.

questions.q: The Indian state with the highest forest cover is?
questions.exp: Madhya Pradesh has the highest total forest cover in India. However, in terms of percentage of total area, Mizoram ranks highest. MP has been consistently the most forested state.

questions.q: Earth Hour is observed in which month?
questions.exp: Earth Hour is observed on the last Saturday of March every year. It is a worldwide movement by WWF where people turn off non-essential electric lights for one hour.

questions.q: The number of biodiversity hotspots in India is?
questions.exp: India has 4 biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland (includes Nicobar Islands). A biodiversity hotspot must have at least 1,500 endemic plant species.
